pageCache.pageTitle: Chilmark and Fonthill Bishop Primary School - Collective Worship
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
All Church maintained schools provide daily collective worship for pupils. In our school this is delivered through whole school, year group or class-based assemblies. This time offers the opportunity to engage in collective expression and reflection, exploring religious, moral and spiritual ideas. Every week there is a Celebration Assembly during which children reflect upon their personal and collective achievement, both in school and outside. We invite parents at the end of each half-term to celebrate their child's achievements, and there is the opportunity for parents to join us for class assemblies.
You have the right to withdraw your child from all or part of the religious education and collective worship provided. If you feel this applies then please come and discuss it with the Headteacher.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chilmark and Fonthill Bishop Primary School - Headteacher's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Headteacher’s Welcome
It is an honour to be the head teacher of this amazing Church of England Primary School.
Chilmark and Fonthill Bishop prides itself on being a happy school where children and adults are encouraged to have a caring, considerate and respectful attitude towards one another. Within a strong Christian ethos, we follow our special words of power which helps pupils and adults, to shine, individually and as a community.
Our engaging curriculum and school values enable children to develop a love of learning and life. We provide an inclusive environment where seeds of learning are planted and children’s skills and knowledge are nourished and allowed to blossom.
Our dedicated staff team work hard resulting in high standards of learning and behaviour. We believe that the education of each individual is most successful when we work in partnership with home. We see parents as active partners in their children’s learning journey and value all that the partnership offers.
If you want to learn more or would like to book a visit, please do not hesitate to contact us.
© 2026 | Legal Information
Website design by Greenhouse School Websites

pageCache.pageTitle: Chilmark and Fonthill Bishop Primary School - Our Collective Worship
pageCache.text:
Our Collective Worship
Collective worship in our school is a daily moment when the whole community gathers as one to reflect, celebrate, and grow together through shared reflection and values. It takes place every day as a whole-school experience and follows carefully planned themes across the academic year, each designed to help children think deeply about themselves, others, and the wider world. Interwoven throughout these themes are our Words of Power — love, friendship, kindness, respect, resilience, faith, and hope — guiding pupils to understand and live out these qualities in their daily lives. Through stories, music, discussion, and quiet thought, collective worship offers opportunities for children to explore spiritual and moral ideas, develop confidence in expressing their beliefs, and appreciate the perspectives of others. At the heart of it all is our vision, ‘Let your light shine’, encouraging every child to recognise their unique gifts and use them to make a positive difference in their community and beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chilmark and Fonthill Bishop Primary School - Our Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Our Vision and Values
“No one lights a lamp and puts it under a bowl; instead it is put on the lampstand, where it gives light for everyone in the house. In the same way your light must shine before people, so that they will see the good things you do and praise your Father in heaven.”
Matthew 5:15-16 (GNT)
Our shared vision is that every child who leaves this school will have had a high-quality education and gained the skills to become a life-long learner; they will have developed values, based on Christian ethics, which will inspire them to play a valuable part in their personal, family and community lives.
Our aim is to be an outstanding school at the heart of the community, promoting Christian values and providing high quality education where the needs of the children are always the primary concern.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chilmark and Fonthill Bishop Primary School - Promoting British Values
pageCache.text:
Promoting British Values
We promote ‘British Values’ through our spiritual, moral, social and cultural education (see SMSC) which permeates through the school’s curriculum and supports the development of the ‘whole child’.
We recognise that such development is most successful when those values and attitudes are promoted by all the staff and provide a model of behaviour for our pupils.
The curriculum in all phases offers broad and balanced opportunities.
For more information click the icons below.
‘British Values’ have been identified as:
Promoting-British-Values (ID 1033)
Democracy
Democracy
The ability to understand and communicate are the most important areas of learning. We ensure that pupils are given a “voice” to communicate. This ‘“voice” could be using words, objects, photographs, pictures, symbols, signing, eye pointing or body language.
We empower our pupils by giving them opportunities to make choices about the things that they believe to be important. By valuing each “voice” and by listening and responding to that voice we demonstrate that we support democracy and liberty.
We have an active School Council.
Individual Liberty
Individual Liberty
Pupils are encouraged to become good and valued citizens. We do this by supporting each pupil to become as independent as possible. We endeavour to demonstrate that everyone has rights; this includes the right to say ‘Yes’ or ‘No’ to ideas or activities. Many of our pupils will be able to take responsibility for particular roles and to understand that with certain rights comes certain responsibilities. Learning to do things independently is an important part of learning to understand yourself. We support others by participating in charitable events such as Red Nose Day/Comic Relief and Children in Need. We believe that engendering a caring and helpful environment and being independent can boost and nurture a healthy self-esteem.
Mutual Respect
Mutual Respect
We promote each pupil’s inclusion in activities, settings and locations that are appropriate to them individually to meet their needs. Within school, pupils work with a range of people and interactions with others are always positively promoted. This may include working with external coaches, theatre groups etc. The curriculum is personalised and planned for pupils and may include transitioning within the range of resources and places on the site and going into the community to meet with a range of people in a variety of situations which include community events and shared participation with other schools/colleges.
We believe it is important to facilitate opportunities to be part of the community as the pupils, families and staff have much to offer in the development of community cohesion.
Rule of Law ,
Rule of Law
We involve pupils in setting codes of behaviour; helping pupils to make decisions and choices that are acceptable to the school community and society at large.
Pupils are helped to learn to manage their behaviour and take responsibility for their actions. Staff are committed to providing a consistent and predictable environment within the school and beyond. We can help many pupils to understand the connection between actions and consequences. This type of environment enables pupils to feel safe and secure; this in turn, promotes the optimum conditions for learning to take place.
We are part of a school and local community where each person is respected and valued equally without regard to ability, gender, faith, heritage or race.
Cultural appreciation and development forms part of our curriculum. We place great emphasis on providing encounters and participation in events and celebrations to broaden all pupils’ experiences and awareness of others.
Our Collective Worship helps all pupils to find out about themselves and others linking their lives to the communities in which they belong.
Pupils are encouraged to experience British Culture through our curriculum themes. For example, pupils have visited many local places. As a school, we take part in sporting activities which helps to instil ‘fair play’ and engender a ‘team spirit’.
Although some of our pupils may find it difficult to articulate their feelings and concerns; staff are attuned to changes in demeanour and well-being that may indicate anxiety. If they are concerned about a pupil our accepted practice links to the Child Protection Policy which entrusts a duty of care to all staff to actively protect and promote the welfare of children.
The staff work closely with parents, carers and other professionals to ensure that the pupils at Chilmark and Fonthill Bishop Primary are happy, well cared for and enabled to learn the skills they need to live a fulfilling life as part of their community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chilmark and Fonthill Bishop Primary School - Parents in Partnership (PiP)
pageCache.text:
Parents in Partnership
At Chilmark and Fonthill Bishop Primary School, we believe that it is essential to develop strong partnerships with home if our children are to achieve their full potential. Parents and schools working as partners can only increase pupil achievement and help to develop positive attitudes about self and school.
One of the ways that we achieve this is to provide regular opportunities for parents to come and engage with visiting experts and members of our own school community on topics of interest. For example: we have hosted talks on Internet safety, Emotional School Based Avoidance, Dyslexia, Mental Wellbeing, Early Reading and SEND.
We have called these sessions PIP (Parents In Partnership). These are advertised termly throughout the year and all members of the community are welcome to join us, for coffee and cake.
The PiP is a great forum for us to share insights into how the school works and we are keen for parents to suggest themes for these sessions. Please contact the school office on admin@chilmarkfonthillbishop.wilts.sch.uk if you have any recommendations for us to address.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chilmark and Fonthill Bishop Primary School - Music
pageCache.text:
Music
Chilmark and Fonthill Bishop provides a vibrant musical education. Pupils learn to play and sing as part of the curriculum. To ensure high quality we employ a specialist music teacher for whole class recorder lessons and whole class singing.
In addition we are able to offer a variety of extra-curricular, low-cost music lessons in school. We can arrange teachers for the following instruments: drums, keyboard, vocal coaching, guitar or brass. These are available on request and booked through the Wiltshire Music Service.
Pupils sing at our Church and also take part in performances throughout the year such as a nativity, musical plays, or celebration assemblies. Chilmark pupils are encouraged to be courageous, brave and in the spotlight. This allows all pupils to develop a confident and self-assured sense of themselves and their place in the world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chilmark and Fonthill Bishop Primary School - School Day
pageCache.text:
School Day
We are open Monday-Friday, term-time only. For our Term Dates please click here.
The official school day begins with doors opening at 8.30am and ends at 3pm.
The total school open hours per week is 32.5 hours.
Our School Day
Our day starts at 8.30am when our school doors open. Registration takes place at 8.40am and the children then start their morning lessons.
We have a 15-minute whole school break at 10.30am. All of Reception and Key Stage One are provided with a free fruit snack. Milk is provided for free to those under 5; older children can have milk if it is ordered and paid for via the school office.
Our in-house cook provides hot lunches on a 3-week rotation, under the guidance of Educatering, who are responsible for our menus containing healthy, nutritious and sustainable choices. For more information click here. or visit www.educatering.uk
School meals are free for children in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2.
We run a variety of free lunchtime clubs, for children who would like to attend.
Our day ends at 3pm unless your child has signed up to one of our after school clubs that run from 3-4pm. Provision of these clubs changes depending on demand and season.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chilmark and Fonthill Bishop Primary School - Open the Book
pageCache.text:
Open the Book
“A Bible story well told has the power to spark the imagination, inspire exploration, give hope, create a smile, teach important lessons and connect generations.”
Source: www.biblesociety.org.uk
Open the Book (OtB) is an exciting storytelling project where Bible stories are shared with children in a way that is fun, interactive and memorable. A group of storytelling volunteers, including two of our governors: Caroline Marking and Grant Philpott, use the Open the Book programme, a drama programme from Bible Society designed to bring bible stories to life for primary school age children, to prepare and present a 10–15-minute scripted Bible story to a school assembly, involving the children as much as possible.
The volunteers are made up of trained and safely recruited from local churches and organisations, who sign up as members and follow the Open the Book Code of Practice.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chilmark and Fonthill Bishop Primary School - Wiltshire Healthy Schools
pageCache.text:
Wiltshire Healthy Schools
Chilmark and Fonthill Bishop Primary School have signed up to Wiltshire Healthy Schools, a Wiltshire Council programme provided to present a joined-up approach to support schools address the health and wellbeing of all young people.
We are “working towards” meeting the standards and as we progress we will be accredited with bronze, silver and then gold levels of attainment.
The programme clarifies the actions all schools can take to promote the health and wellbeing of young people, from universal prevention and education to targeted interventions and treatment. The programme brings together good practice on all health-related issues and provides consistent messages, encouraging and supporting schools to focus on approaches that are particularly effective.
The Wiltshire Healthy Schools Standards have been developed to meet the health priorities and needs of the children and young people of Wiltshire. The Standards are linked to the current Ofsted Common Inspection Framework, national and local Public Health Outcomes and other guidance for schools including from NICE (National Institute of health and Care Excellence).

pageCache.pageTitle: Chilmark and Fonthill Bishop Primary School - Governors
pageCache.text:
Our Governors
Governors are volunteers who work with the headteacher and senior leadership team to drive the strategic development of the school and raise standards of achievement. Duties include setting the school's vision, aims and objectives, approving the school budget and holding the headteacher to account.
Our Governors (ID 1105)
Caroline Marking
I have been involved with the school for more than 5 years. I am Chair of Governors and am the Governor who has responsibility for Safeguarding and SEND. I am also the link Governor for Early Year's Foundation Stage (EYFS), History and Geography.
I was previously a Governor of a Prep School in Salisbury for several years and have recently taken up a role at the new Salisbury Academy for Inspirational Learning (SAIL). I am a Trustee of the Pembroke Centre which is the home of Wilton Riding for the Disabled which aims to enrich lives through involvement with horses. I have three children and live in Fonthill Gifford.
Grant Philpott
I am an engineer and have spent most of my working life in the area of patenting. I am married to Morag and we have lived in wonderful Chilmark for 8 years. We have three adult children who grew up and were educated in the UK, Germany, The Netherlands and Brazil, so we have experience of various educational systems, and their strengths and weaknesses. I also set up and led the Duke of Edinburgh's Award together with a team of around 20 teachers and parents at the European School in Munich. I have been a governor in Chilmark for around 2 years and thoroughly enjoy the role – I look forward to meeting you!
Sally Naish
Linda Evans
Camilla Woodward
Rebecca Murphy
Anne Martin
Millie Fox
Ruth Blamey
Ruth Blamey
I moved to Teffont Evias in April 2010 with my husband Richard and our cockerpoo Lola, but I continued to work in London until December 2024 when I partially retired. The first 15 years of my career were spent working in various senior finance roles in the hotel industry (Holiday Inns, InterContinental Hotels, and The Savoy Group). This was followed by 20 years working with SMEs in media, events, conferences & training industries, where I enjoyed the ability to affect change more quickly in smaller organisations. All roles involved restructuring, innovating, and managing teams, reporting to the Board of Directors, and covered responsibility for IT, HR, legal and office facilities management.
In May 2026 I joined Chilmark School as the Finance Governor helping to implement and maintain strong financial policies and procedures. In April 2026 I was also co-opted onto the Teffont Parochial Church Council to work as Treasurer of the “Friends of Evias Church”, an appeal to raise funds to restore the church of St Michael and All Angels.
